To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
undernutrition during the brain growth spurt leads to a reduced capacity of the brain to form myelin and to synthesize neurotransmitters.
early postnatal under-nourishment of the rat results in a reduced brain weight and a reduced brain DNA content.
undernutrition during the brain growth spurt leads to deficits in the glial population, and reduced development in cellular processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of undernutrition on the brain growth-spur...
the effects of undernutrition on the brain of the rat.
the effect of undernutrition during the brain growth spurt on the development of the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of early undernutrition are not confined to the brain but extend to the whole organism, and that they are not limited to the period of brain growth-spurt.

early postnatal malnutrition leads to a reduction in the number of cells in the brain, and to a reduction in their ability to synthesize and to secrete the macromolecules required for their development and for the development of the myelin sheath.
the brain of the undernurished rat is less well developed, both in terms of cellular and biochemical parameters, than the brain of the normally-nourished animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain growth-spur is an essential period for the formation of the brain and that any interference with the normal supply of nutrients to the fetus or the suckling will result in a deficit in brain size and function.
early postnatal under-nourishment results in a reduction of the number and size of the neurons, and of the number of glial cells.
early undernutrition has long-lasting effects on the development of the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of undernutrition are not confined to the period during which it is applied, and that they persist throughout the life of the animal, even though it is well-nourished as an adult.
early life nutritional status can have a long-term impact on the brain and can affect cognitive function.
the brain is not a static organ, but is constantly changing in its structure, function, and metabolism.
